summary.text: A 35 year old woman with no significant past history developed a 24 h history of gross hematuria, generalized weakness and decreased urine outflow. She had recently been diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B and D infection and was receiving weekly subcutaneous pegylated interferon. On initial evaluation she had severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, severe obstructive acute kidney injury and mild coagulopathy, with ultrasonography showing a distended bladder with a large intravesical mass consistent with clot retention.

She underwent urgent hemodialysis twice and emergency rigid cystoscopy with clot evacuation, which found a diffuse mucosal ooze without a discrete bleeding source. Catheter irrigation resolved the hematuria and she was discharged after 48 h, but within 48 h severe gross hematuria, clots, lethargy and recurrent severe anemia returned, requiring three units of red cells and empiric intravenous ceftriaxone.

Multiphasic CT urogram showed a left superior and a right inferior vesical artery pseudoaneurysm, confirmed by selective pelvic angiography; bladder neoplasia and vascular malformations were excluded. Emergent embolization used microcoils on the left and polyvinyl alcohol particles on the right, with completion angiography showing exclusion of both lesions.

Hematuria subsided within 12 h of embolization, the urinary catheter was withdrawn on the second postoperative day, hemoglobin was 10.1 g/dL and creatinine 0.8 mg/dL before discharge, and at the six-week visit she was asymptomatic with complete thrombosis and regression of both pseudoaneurysms on imaging.
